910.name: Ligurian & Greek Settlements
910.description: The Rock of Monaco was first settled by Ligurian tribes and later became associated with the Greek colony of Massalia (Marseille). The name 'Monaco' may derive from the Greek Monoikos, linked to the Hercules Monoikos temple.

sub_clusters.name: Ligurian & Phocaean Greek Presence
sub_clusters.description: Ligurian habitation of the rocky headland, Phocaean Greek trading contacts, the temple of Hercules Monoikos, and eventual Roman incorporation.

920.name: Grimaldi Seizure & Genoese Era
920.description: The Genoese built a fortress on the Rock in 1215. In 1297, François Grimaldi, disguised as a Franciscan monk, seized the fortress—an event commemorated on Monaco's coat of arms. The Grimaldi dynasty has ruled ever since.

sub_clusters.name: Genoese Fortress Construction
sub_clusters.description: Genoa's construction of a fortress colony on the Rock of Monaco as part of Guelph-Ghibelline rivalry, and the strategic importance of the position overlooking the western Mediterranean.

sub_clusters.name: Grimaldi Seizure of Monaco (1297)
sub_clusters.description: François Grimaldi's capture of the fortress disguised as a monk (8 January 1297), the subsequent Grimaldi struggles to maintain control, and recognition of Grimaldi sovereignty.
key_events: François Grimaldi seizes Monaco fortress disguised as a monk (1297)

930.name: Spanish & French Protectorates
930.description: Monaco navigated between great powers through a series of protectorate arrangements—first with Spain (1524–1641), then France (1641–1793)—before being annexed by Revolutionary France.

sub_clusters.name: Spanish Protectorate Era
sub_clusters.description: Monaco under Spanish protection following the Treaty of Tordesillas, the Grimaldis as Spanish vassals, and the strategic role of Monaco's harbour in Mediterranean naval warfare.

sub_clusters.name: French Protectorate & Treaty of Péronne
sub_clusters.description: Honoré II's switch to French protection via the Treaty of Péronne (1641), gaining the title of Prince, French cultural influence, and annexation by Revolutionary France in 1793.
key_events: Treaty of Péronne establishes French protectorate over Monaco (1641)

940.name: Restoration & Monte Carlo Casino
940.description: The Grimaldis were restored after Napoleon's fall, but Monaco lost Menton and Roquebrune to Sardinia/France. Prince Charles III's founding of the Monte Carlo Casino (1863) transformed the impoverished principality into a glamorous resort.

sub_clusters.name: Grimaldi Restoration & Territorial Loss
sub_clusters.description: Restoration of the Grimaldis under Sardinian protection (1815), the loss of Menton and Roquebrune (seceded 1848, sold to France 1861), reducing Monaco to its present tiny territory.

sub_clusters.name: Monte Carlo Casino Founding
sub_clusters.description: Charles III's creation of the Société des Bains de Mer (1856), the opening of the Monte Carlo Casino (1863), abolition of income tax thanks to casino revenues, and Monaco's emergence as a playground for European aristocracy.
key_events: Monte Carlo Casino opens, transforming Monaco's economy (1863)

950.name: World Wars & Rainier III's Modernisation
950.description: Monaco navigated both World Wars with varying degrees of neutrality and occupation. Prince Rainier III's ascension in 1949 and his marriage to Grace Kelly in 1956 launched Monaco's modern era of glamour and economic diversification.

sub_clusters.name: WWI, WWII & Italian-German Occupation
sub_clusters.description: Monaco's nominal neutrality in WWI, Italian occupation (1942), German occupation (1943), and liberation in 1944, alongside the constitutional crisis of 1911 and Albert I's oceanographic work.

sub_clusters.name: Rainier III & Grace Kelly
sub_clusters.description: Rainier III's accession, the fairy-tale marriage to Hollywood actress Grace Kelly (1956), the 1962 constitutional reform establishing a parliamentary monarchy, and the confrontation with de Gaulle over taxation.
key_events: Prince Rainier III marries Grace Kelly (1956)

960.name: Modern Sovereign Microstate
960.description: Contemporary Monaco as a sovereign microstate characterised by the Formula 1 Grand Prix, tax-haven status, land reclamation, luxury tourism, and the Grimaldi dynasty's continued reign under Albert II.

sub_clusters.name: F1 Grand Prix & Luxury Brand
sub_clusters.description: The Monaco Grand Prix as an iconic Formula 1 event, the principality's brand as a luxury destination, land reclamation projects (Fontvieille), and the death of Princess Grace (1982).

sub_clusters.name: Albert II & Contemporary Era
sub_clusters.description: Prince Albert II's accession (2005), focus on environmental issues and ocean conservation, Monaco's admission to the Council of Europe, ongoing controversies over tax-haven status, and the €2 billion Portier Cove land extension.
key_events: Prince Albert II accedes to the throne (2005)

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
